c2.title: No-look-ahead discipline
c2.imperative: Confirm recent_history_baseline uses only the same driver's strictly earlier rounds in the same season.
c2.finding: build_quali_error_table sorts gaps by [year, driver_id, round_num] before groupby([year, driver_id])['actual_pace_gap'].transform(lambda s: s.shift(1).expanding().mean()). shift(1) excludes the current round's own value; expanding().mean() averages only rows at or before the shifted position, i.e. strictly earlier rounds. groupby key includes year, so no cross-season carryover -- confirmed no year-to-year leakage. No lookahead: the first round of each driver's season has NaN baseline and is dropped (175 rows, printed and matches G1_FINDINGS.md).

c3.title: Join-grain correctness
c3.imperative: Confirm the constructor-to-driver broadcast is correct (no many-to-many duplication/silent drop); cross-check row-count arithmetic.
c3.finding: Independent SQL check on data/physics_estimates.db: SELECT year,round_idx,constructor,COUNT(*) FROM session_estimates WHERE session_type='Q' GROUP BY ... HAVING COUNT(*)>1 returns ZERO duplicate keys; distinct (year,round_idx,constructor) key count (1597) exactly equals total row count (1597) -- the join's right-hand side is provably unique, so merge(..., how='inner') cannot duplicate rows, only drop unmatched left rows. Script's own printed counts confirm no drop occurred either (2985 quali_error rows in -> 2985 after join, 0 unresolved). This is confirmed structurally, not just by arithmetic approximation.

c4.title: Team-name reconciliation vs canonicalize_team_name
c4.imperative: Independently verify team_canonicalization.py would misjoin here, and spot-check the script's own reconciliation for known rebrand cases.
c4.finding: Read src/evo_predictor/team_canonicalization.py directly: _TEAM_ALIAS_MAP = {'alfa romeo': 'Kick Sauber', 'alphatauri': 'RB'} is a flat, year-agnostic dict with no year parameter anywhere in canonicalize_team_name's signature. Independently simulated it against real DB values: in 2021 and 2023, session_classifications.team='Alfa Romeo' (exact) canonicalizes to 'Kick Sauber', but session_estimates.constructor for those years is 'Alfa Romeo Racing'(2021)/'Alfa Romeo'(2023) -- 'Kick Sauber' does not appear in session_estimates until 2024. Reusing canonicalize_team_name for this join direction would therefore silently drop/misjoin all pre-2024 Alfa Romeo rows -- the implementer's claim is CONFIRMED, not just plausible. Separately, spot-checked the script's own match_constructor logic against all 94 distinct team labels across 2019-2026 (Alfa Romeo/Kick Sauber, AlphaTauri/RB/Racing Bulls, Racing Point/Aston Martin, Renault/Alpine, plus every other team) -- zero unresolved, matching the implementer's verification run.

triage_candidates.statement: src/evo_predictor/team_canonicalization.py::canonicalize_team_name is year-agnostic and would misjoin pre-2024 Alfa Romeo rows if reused for the session_estimates<->session_classifications join direction (confirmed live: 2021/2023 team='Alfa Romeo' canonicalizes to 'Kick Sauber', which does not exist as a session_estimates constructor before 2024). Worth a Cartographer note or a follow-up issue if any other future consumer needs this join direction, so the next implementer doesn't rediscover it from scratch.

Team-level->driver-level physics broadcast (both teammates share identical constructor-level physics axis values) dilutes any true per-driver signal; the implementer already flagged this in G1_FINDINGS.md as a documented Phase-0 simplification, not an error, but a per-driver physics estimate (if the estimator is ever extended) would be a stronger test than this constructor-broadcast measurement can currently detect.
